basis: corrective re-do of round 2 (all 10 rejected). Zee: "My drawing was super rough, i expected you to take that as a guide not exactly." Every S here is constructed from computed geometry; no traced path is reused.

logos.r3-01: Two layers stay, but the S is rebuilt as a real two-circle letterform and the tiles drop back to a quiet teal ground in two solid tints. The letter leads; the layers give it depth.
logos.r3-02: The two tiles become the S’s own terminals — one anchoring each end of the letter, so the two layers ARE the two halves coming into register.
logos.r3-03: The gap is the idea: two halves approaching sync but not yet touching. Tiles dropped entirely — the split alone carries the meaning. Two elements.
logos.r3-04: Drawn the way a typeface draws an S: smaller upper bowl, larger lower bowl, lighter stroke above and heavier below. Proper letterform stress, not a symmetric loop.
logos.r3-05: The curve language swapped for the tiles’ straight edges — an angular S cut from horizontals and verticals. Modern and sharp; softened only at the joints. Honest caveat: at 24px it can read as a 5 before it reads as an S.
logos.r3-06: Figure/ground flip: the S is cut OUT of the front tile, with the second layer showing through behind. Honest retest of the knockout idea now that the letter is properly built.
logos.r3-07: Two identical waves running in phase — the brief’s tuning-fork territory. No letter at all: sync shown as two signals matched rather than as an S. Honest caveat: it reads as a wave mark, not as a B or an S.
logos.r3-08: No letter at all: two tiles overlapping, and the register point where they lock marked as a turned square. Sync as a mechanical click.
logos.r3-09: Three bars snapping into register, offset right-centre-left so the rhythm alone spells the S. Layers stacking — the simplest reading at 24px. Honest caveat: staggered bars are close to a text-align or menu icon.
logos.r3-10: Two nodes joined by one S-curve link — sync as connection, at the lowest element count in the batch. Survives smallest.
